A validated symptom and quality-of-life measure
The activity the patient wants back

title: Timing after prostate treatment

At least twelve months for mild–moderate SUI
Surgery may be offered for bothersome, non-improving SUI despite conservative care
Offer surgery for persisting bothersome SUI

title: Pump use over time
label: Pump assessment
items: Watch the patient operate a demonstration pump
Check reach, strength and understanding
Agree an accessible position before surgery
Consider future frailty and loss of independence

title: Flexible cystoscopy before implantation
cols: AUA recommends cystourethroscopy before SUI surgery
BAUS selects cystoscopy within its VUDS pathway
Advance inspection is a practical preference
bottom: Suspected narrowing needs definition. Unplanned dilation can obscure the decision.

title: Urodynamics: BAUS, EAU and AUA
rows: UDS before invasive treatment, weak recommendation
UDS when diagnosis or counselling benefits
State the uncertainty the test should resolve
bottom: The key question: which result would change the treatment or counselling?

title: Interpreting an imperfect study
rows: Urine, bladder diary, free flow and repeated residual
Storage safety, emptying and outlet stability
bottom: Low capacity can reflect leakage. A weak laboratory contraction needs the real voiding history.

title: Consent: improvement and lifetime burden
bottom: Different endpoints and populations. These figures do not compare device efficacy. Consent includes future revision, erosion and residual leakage.

title: Case 1: six pads and urgency
facts: Goal: walk without soaking his clothes
question: Implant now or optimise first?
bottom: DO alone need not exclude general AUS surgery. ContiClassic labelling requires bladder conditions to be controlled or resolved.

title: Urgency treatment and emptying
rows: Address reversible contributors and symptom burden
Choose medication with cognition and residual urine in mind
Plan retention and repeated access before botulinum toxin
Treat persistent urgency as a separate outcome after AUS
bottom: No universally superior treatment sequence around a cuff has been established.

title: Case 2: weak contraction and residual urine
facts: Obstruction and test inhibition remain possible
question: Would a reliable emptying plan change your answer?
bottom: Selected DU cohorts do not establish safety in unresolved retention. There is no universal residual cutoff.

title: Catheterisation with a cuff in place
items: Establish the reason and likely frequency of catheterisation
Test competence and agree the drainage route before implantation
Plan repeated or prolonged access with specialist input
bottom: Follow the actual device instructions before instrumentation. No universal French-size rule applies.

title: Detrusor overactivity and poor compliance
bottom: Schematic traces only, with arbitrary units. Confirm trace quality and assess renal function or upper tracts when indicated.

title: Three different sites of narrowing
label: Anatomical distinctions
items: Anterior stricture: urethra and spongiosum
Bladder-neck contracture: prostate partly present
VUAS: anastomosis after radical prostatectomy
bottom: Symptoms, flow, residual and anatomy must support a stable outlet.

title: Reassessment and urethral stability
rows: Interval cystoscopy after symptomatic BNC/VUAS treatment
At least six months without recurrence
bottom: These intervals describe different pathways. Recurrence pattern, tissue quality and future access remain decisive.

title: Case 3: radiation and recurrent VUAS
facts: Patency still depends on further intervention
question: Implant, stage reconstruction or reconsider the endpoint?
bottom: A specialist reconstructive plan comes first. Radiation-associated risk estimates do not give a personal probability of failure.

title: AUS after urethral reconstruction
cols: Prior erosion, graft or posterior reconstruction
Reassess unsafe planes or stage the procedure
bottom: New observational data support a detailed history, without proving one reconstructive technique superior.

title: Transcorporal placement: role and costs
cols: A compromised urethra with a hazardous dorsal plane
A manoeuvre addressing a defined dissection problem
Sexual consequences and future prosthesis surgery
Confounding by indication in comparative series
bottom: Tandem cuffs and other salvage procedures require a specific indication and specialist judgement.

title: The fifteen-minute wash question
lead: No direct AUS outcome evidence establishes a fixed 15-minute preparation
rows: Correct product, site, contact and drying
bottom: BAUS’s five-minute topical field scrub is consensus with extrapolation. Product timings address different activities.

title: Skin culture reduction and clinical infection
bottom: Yeung 2013: 100 initial GU prosthetic procedures, 50 per arm. Immediate skin cultures, not AUS infection or a duration trial.

title: Urine and antibiotic disagreements
rows: BAUS urine pathway and IDSA’s AUS-specific position differ
Complete before incision and plan appropriate redosing
Observational AUS data show no convincing benefit. The retrieved ContiClassic IFU describes a longer regimen.
bottom: Verify current regional labelling and agree a documented local microbiology and implant-service protocol.

title: Contamination control during implantation
label: Handling sequence
items: Protect the implant until the field is ready
Limit skin contact and unnecessary handling
Use fresh sterile gloves and a clean handling pause
Separate irrigation, device dipping and internal filling
bottom: Bundle studies cannot isolate the benefit of each component. Compatibility remains device-specific.

title: Balloon pocket and pressure selection
bottom: A safe pocket and the correct pressure component are separate decisions. Fill volumes and selection rules require the current OR protocol.

cols: Early catheter removal when appropriate, with verified emptying

title: Case 4: leakage after three good years
facts: Leakage mechanism and pump use still need assessment
Erosion, mechanics and bladder dysfunction remain possible
question: What would you investigate before choosing revision?
bottom: Urethral atrophy requires investigation. Time alone does not justify cuff downsizing or pressure escalation.

Future access belongs in the operative plan
